item.title: Standing to one side, the deity Tayana recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One: O brahmin, striving, cut the stream, Abandon and…
item.description:
Standing to one side, the deity Tayana recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

O brahmin, striving, cut the stream,
Abandon and destroy
All clinging to sensual desires.
Without cutting sensual desires,
A sage cannot attain unification of mind.
If you do what should be done,
Be steadfast and energetic.
If a goer-forth is lazy,
He scatters even more dust.
Not doing is better than doing badly —
Doing badly leads to suffering afterward.
Having done, do it well —
Doing well brings no suffering.
Like holding grass the wrong way,
It can cut your hand,
So too, the ascetic life wrongly practiced
Drags one to hell.
Any lazy conduct,
Any defiled practice,
Any evil action in the holy life
Does not yield great fruit.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.8

item.title: “Monks, defilement is a disease; defilement is a boil; defilement is a dart. Therefore, monks, the Tathāgata dwells without defilement, free from the dart. Therefore,…
item.description:
“Monks, defilement is a disease; defilement is a boil; defilement is a dart. Therefore, monks, the Tathāgata dwells without defilement, free from the dart. Therefore, monks, if any monk has a wish, let him wish to dwell without defilement, free from the dart. Do not conceive about the eye, do not conceive in the eye, do not conceive from the eye, do not conceive ‘the eye is mine.’ Do not conceive about forms … Do not conceive about eye-consciousness … Do not conceive about eye-contact … Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact … do not conceive about that feeling, do not conceive in it, do not conceive from it, do not conceive ‘that feeling is mine.’ Do not conceive about everything, do not conceive in everything, do not conceive from everything, do not conceive ‘everything is mine.’ Not conceiving thus, he does not cling to anything in the world. Not clinging, he is not agitated. Not agitated, he personally attains Nibbāna. He knows: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.90

item.title: “If there were no gratification in form, monks, beings would not become lustful for form. But because there is gratification in form, beings become lustful…
item.description:
“If there were no gratification in form, monks, beings would not become lustful for form. But because there is gratification in form, beings become lustful for form. If there were no peril in form, beings would not become disenchanted with form. But because there is peril in form, beings become disenchanted with form. If there were no escape from form, beings would not escape from form. But because there is escape from form, beings escape from form. Monks, as long as beings do not directly know as it actually is the gratification as gratification, the peril as peril, the escape as escape in regard to these six internal sense bases, they have not, monks, along with this world of devas, Māras, Brahmās, with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans, dwelt with minds free from clinging, detached, liberated, unbounded. But because beings have directly known them as they actually are, therefore they have dwelt with minds free from clinging, detached, liberated, unbounded.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.18
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Rādha, whatever form there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all form should…
item.description:
“Rādha, whatever form there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all form should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever feeling … perception … formations … consciousness there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all consciousness should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Rādha, knowing thus, seeing thus, regarding this conscious body and all external signs, there is no ‘I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.71
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Again, the five kinds of kings Are present in the world — Learn to subdue them, Always keeping mindfulness. Toward forms and sounds, Toward tastes…
item.description:
“Again, the five kinds of kings
Are present in the world —
Learn to subdue them,
Always keeping mindfulness.
Toward forms and sounds,
Toward tastes and smells,
And toward contacts —
Subdue desire and lust.

Subdue desire
For these things.
The mindful monk,
With mind well liberated,
Then, at the right time,
Rightly reflecting on the Dhamma,
With unified mind,
He should destroy darkness.” So spoke the Blessed One.

From: Sutta Nipāta 4.16

item.title: - What is called the wrong path? What destroys day and night? What defiles the holy life? What is a bath without water? - Greed…
item.description:
- What is called the wrong path?
What destroys day and night?
What defiles the holy life?
What is a bath without water?
- Greed is called the wrong path,
Aging destroys day and night,
Women defile the holy life,
Ensnaring humankind —
Austerities and the holy life
Are a bath without water.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.58

item.title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen factors of enlightenment arise and arisen factors of enlightenment come to completion, as wise…
item.description:
“I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen factors of enlightenment arise and arisen factors of enlightenment come to completion, as wise attention. Through wise attention, monks, unarisen factors of enlightenment arise and arisen factors of enlightenment come to full development.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.75

item.title: “Venerable sir, what is the first jhāna?” “Here, venerable sir, a monk, secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the…
item.description:
“Venerable sir, what is the first jhāna?” “Here, venerable sir, a monk, secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, accompanied by initial and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. This, venerable sir, is called the first jhāna.” “Venerable sir, how many factors does the first jhāna have?” “Venerable sir, the first jhāna has five factors. Here, a monk in the first jhāna has initial thought, sustained thought, rapture, pleasure, and unification of mind. Thus, venerable sir, the first jhāna has five factors.” “Venerable sir, how many factors does the first jhāna abandon and how many does it possess?” “Venerable sir, the first jhāna abandons five factors and possesses five factors. Here, a monk in the first jhāna has abandoned sensual desire, abandoned ill-will, abandoned sloth and torpor, abandoned restlessness and remorse, abandoned doubt; he possesses initial thought, sustained thought, rapture, pleasure, and unification of mind. Thus, venerable sir, the first jhāna abandons five factors and possesses five factors.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 43 – Mahāvedallasutta

item.title: “Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving there is for form — abandon it. Thus that form will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made…
item.description:
“Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving there is for form — abandon it. Thus that form will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made non-existent, so that it cannot arise again in the future. Regarding feeling … perception … formations … Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving there is for consciousness — abandon it. Thus that consciousness will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made non-existent, so that it cannot arise again in the future.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 23.9
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, for a clansman who has gone forth out of faith, this is the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma: dwell often in disenchantment toward…
item.description:
“Monks, for a clansman who has gone forth out of faith, this is the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma: dwell often in disenchantment toward form … toward feeling … toward perception … toward formations, dwell often in disenchantment toward consciousness. One who dwells often in disenchantment toward form … toward consciousness fully understands form … feeling … perception … formations … fully understands consciousness. One who fully understands form, fully understands feeling, fully understands perception, fully understands formations, fully understands consciousness, is freed from form, freed from feeling, freed from perception, freed from formations, freed from consciousness, freed from birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. I say that he is freed from suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.146
